name: The Lime of Achterberg
verified_sources: https://bomenbieb.nl/bijzondere-bomen/linde-van-achterberg/
Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen (Bomenstichting), entry nr 1683006, coordinate 26m from bomenbieb's own pin
access: Stands on the former outer bailey (voorburcht) of the demolished Kasteel Levendael, now farmland beside Levendaalselaan; visible from the lane. LRMB records 'visitable: onbekend, visible: ja'. Treat as viewable from the public road pending a firmer access statement.
transport: Village of Achterberg, between Veenendaal and Rhenen; nearest station Veenendaal-De Klomp, then bike/drive (no direct public transport to the door).
verify_notes: Popularly called 'the 1000-year lime of Achterberg', but LRMB's own register entry explicitly disputes this: 'zeker geen 1000 jaar oud... wel wordt ingeschat dat hij meer dan 350 jaar geleden is geplant' (certainly not 1000 years old; estimated planted more than 350 years ago). Girth 603cm. Stood in the outer bailey of Kasteel Levendael; local tradition says justice was dispensed under lindes (Old Germanic custom, 'onder lindes werd rechtgesproken'). The castle was demolished around 1820 and replaced by a farm. By 1922 the tree was well-known enough to be written into the property's deed of sale, obliging owners to preserve it. In 1965 it was slated for felling due to poor condition; the Copijn brothers intervened with tree-surgery techniques that introduced arboriculture as a discipline in the Netherlands. The trunk is now fully hollow with a new stem growing up through the middle. Two independent sources agree: bomenbieb.nl (planted ~1650, alive) and LRMB nr 1683006 (26m coordinate match, same girth-based estimate, no felling language in its history text). RECOMMENDATION: join Ede (7.65km, next free ede_ id) - within the doctrine's day-trip join range, and this is a genuinely good tree (girth, documented legal history, a real conservation story) worth the trip to a small village.

location.neighbourhood: Heure, a hamlet on the Beekvliet estate near Borculo, municipality of Berkelland

verify_notes: Bomenbieb and the LRMB register both call this THE thickest elm in the Netherlands ('de dikste iep van ons land'), a genuine national superlative worth stating plainly and sourcing to the register. It is a European white elm (fladderiep), a species distinguished by deep-grooved plank-buttress roots at the base that give riverbank species like this one and the black poplar extra stability against flooding and wind; the register notes fladderiep is unusually resistant to Dutch elm disease, which has killed most of the country's other elms, adding a real reason this species and this specimen matter. Full, healthy crown, low branches, good vitality per the register. No exact girth figure given in either source despite the superlative claim; note this gap rather than inventing a number. RECOMMENDATION: strong candidate for its own new single-tree place (a national superlative, in a tiny hamlet with no city nearby to join at 27.8km from Enschede, well past the join range) - would somebody travel specifically for the thickest elm in the country?
